p.src: Now Xu Shu hastened on to Xuchang. When Cao Cao learned that he had arrived, he ordered Xun Yu, Cheng Yu, and a company of other advisers to welcome him. Xu Shu entered the chancellor's residence and paid his respects to Cao Cao. Cao Cao said, “You are a man of exceptional wisdom. Why did you lower yourself to serve Liu Bei?” Xu Shu replied, “In my youth I fled from calamity and wandered abroad. By chance I came to Xinye, where I formed a close friendship with Xuande. As my aged mother is here, I am deeply ashamed yet grateful that you were kind enough to consider my circumstances.” Cao Cao said, “Now that you are here, you may attend your honored mother morning and evening, while I too shall have the privilege of hearing your enlightened counsel.”

p.src: Xu Shu bowed his thanks and withdrew. He hurried to see his mother and, weeping, bowed before her below the hall. His mother exclaimed in astonishment, “Why have you come here?” Xu Shu replied, “Recently I was serving Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, in Xinye. When I received your letter, Mother, I traveled here without rest by night and day.” Mother Xu flew into a rage, struck the table, and cursed him: “You disgraceful son! After wandering abroad for several years, I thought your learning would have improved. How is it that you are worse than before? Since you have studied the classics, you should know that loyalty and filial duty cannot always both be fulfilled. Do you not know that Cao Cao is a traitor who deceives his sovereign and defies those above him? Liu Xuande's benevolence and righteousness are renowned throughout the realm, and moreover he is a scion of the imperial house of Han. Having entered his service, you had found a worthy lord. Yet now, on the strength of a single forged letter, without investigating it at all, you have abandoned the light for darkness and brought disgrace upon yourself. What an utter fool you are! How can I have the face to meet you? You have dishonored your ancestors and were born into this world in vain!” So fierce was her denunciation that Xu Shu remained prostrate on the ground, not daring to raise his eyes. His mother turned and went behind the screen.

p.src: When Xu Shu saw that his mother was dead, he wept until he collapsed to the ground and did not revive for a long while. Cao Cao sent gifts of condolence and later came in person to offer sacrifice. Xu Shu buried his mother's coffin on the southern plain outside Xuchang, then observed mourning and kept vigil at her grave. He refused everything Cao Cao bestowed upon him. At that time Cao Cao wished to discuss a southern campaign, but Xun Yu remonstrated, “The weather is cold; this is not yet the time to employ troops. Wait until the warmth of spring; then we may drive deep into the south in full force.” Cao Cao accepted his advice. He diverted water from the Zhang River to form a lake, named it the Black Tortoise Lake, and trained a naval force there in preparation for the southern campaign.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xuande was preparing gifts for a visit to Zhuge Liang at Longzhong when someone suddenly reported, “A gentleman waits outside the gate. He wears a lofty cap and a broad sash and has the extraordinary bearing of a man of the Way. He has come especially to see you.” Xuande said, “Can this be Kongming himself?” He straightened his robes and went out to welcome the visitor. But when he looked, he saw that it was Sima Hui. Overjoyed, Xuande invited him into the rear hall and seated him in the place of honor. Bowing, he said, “Since taking leave of your venerable presence, I have been occupied each day with pressing military affairs and have failed to pay you a visit. Your honored visit today brings the greatest comfort to one who has so long admired you.” Sima Hui said, “I heard that Xu Yuanzhi was here and came especially to meet him.” Xuande replied, “Recently Cao Cao imprisoned his mother, and she sent a messenger with a letter summoning him back to Xuchang. So he has gone.” Sima Hui said, “Then he has fallen into Cao Cao's scheme! I have always heard that Mother Xu is a woman of the highest virtue. Though held captive by Cao Cao, she would certainly never send a letter summoning her son. The letter must have been a forgery. Had Yuanzhi stayed, his mother would have survived; now that he has gone, she will surely die.”

p.src: Startled, Xuande asked why. Sima Hui replied, “Mother Xu's principles are lofty; she will surely be ashamed to face her son.” Xuande said, “Before he left, Yuanzhi recommended Zhuge Liang of Nanyang. What manner of man is he?” Sima Hui laughed. “If Yuanzhi wished to leave, he should simply have gone. Why did he have to draw that man out and make him exhaust his heart's blood?” Xuande asked, “Why do you say that, Master?” Sima Hui replied, “Kongming is a close friend of Cui Zhouping of Boling, Shi Guangyuan of Yingchuan, Meng Gongwei of Runan, and Xu Yuanzhi. Those four apply themselves to mastering particular fields, while Kongming alone surveys the larger design. Once, as he sat clasping his knees and chanting at length, he pointed to the four and said, ‘If you gentlemen enter official service, you may rise to be provincial inspectors or commandery governors.’ When they asked what Kongming himself aspired to, he merely smiled and gave no answer. He has always compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi. His abilities are beyond measure.” Xuande said, “Why does Yingchuan produce so many worthy men?” Sima Hui replied, “Long ago, Yin Kui, who was skilled in observing the heavens, once said that the stars gathered over the celestial division of Ying; therefore that land was certain to produce many worthy men.”

p.src: Guan Yu, who was standing nearby, said, “I have heard that Guan Zhong and Yue Yi were renowned men of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, whose achievements overshadowed the whole world. Is it not excessive for Kongming to compare himself to these two?” Sima Hui laughed. “In my view, he should not be compared to those two. I would compare him instead to two other men.” Guan Yu asked which two he meant. Sima Hui replied, “He may be compared to Jiang Ziya, who established the Zhou for eight hundred years, and Zhang Zifang, who brought prosperity to the Han for four hundred years.” Everyone was astonished. Sima Hui descended the steps, took his leave, and prepared to depart. Xuande tried to detain him, but could not. Outside the gate, Sima Hui threw back his head and laughed aloud. “Though Sleeping Dragon has found his lord, he has not found his time. What a pity!” With that, he drifted away with an air of freedom. p.src: Xuande reached the manor, dismounted, and personally knocked at the brushwood gate. A young boy came out and asked his business. Xuande said, “Liu Bei, Left General of the Han, Marquis of Yicheng Village, Governor of Yuzhou, and Imperial Uncle, has come especially to pay his respects to the master.” The boy said, “I cannot remember so many names and titles.” Xuande said, “Just tell him that Liu Bei came to visit.” The boy replied, “The master went out early this morning.” Xuande asked, “Where did he go?” The boy replied, “His movements are uncertain. I do not know where he went.” Xuande asked, “When will he return?” The boy replied, “The time of his return is uncertain too. It may be three or five days, or perhaps ten days or more.”

p.src: Xuande was deeply disappointed. Zhang Fei said, “Since we cannot see him, let us simply go home.” Xuande replied, “Let us wait a little while.” Guan Yu said, “It would be better to return for now and send someone later to make inquiries.” Xuande accepted his advice and instructed the boy, “If the master returns, tell him that Liu Bei came to pay him a visit.” He then mounted his horse. After traveling several li, he reined in and looked back at the scenery of Longzhong. Truly, the mountains were not high, yet graceful; the waters not deep, yet limpid. The land was not broad, yet level; the woods not vast, yet luxuriant. Apes and cranes lived peaceably together, while pines and bamboo mingled their green. He could not cease admiring the view. Suddenly he saw a man approaching along a secluded mountain path, leaning on a staff of chenopod. He had an imposing countenance and a handsome, spirited bearing, with a carefree scholar's cap upon his head and a black cloth robe upon his body. Xuande said, “This must be Master Sleeping Dragon.” He hurriedly dismounted, went forward to salute him, and asked, “Sir, are you not Sleeping Dragon?” The man replied, “Who are you, General?” Xuande said, “I am Liu Bei.” The man said, “I am not Kongming. I am Kongming's friend, Cui Zhouping of Boling.” Xuande said, “I have long heard your distinguished name and am fortunate to meet you. May I ask you to sit here on the ground for a moment and grant me a word of instruction?”

p.src: The two men sat facing each other upon a stone in the woods, while Guan Yu and Zhang Fei stood attending at Liu Bei’s side. Zhou Ping asked, “Why does the general wish to see Kongming?” Xuande replied, “The realm is now in great disorder, with turmoil rising on every side. I wish to see Kongming and ask him for a plan to bring peace to the realm and stability to the state.” Zhou Ping laughed. “Your chief purpose is to quell the disorder. Benevolent though that intention is, order and chaos have never remained constant since ancient times. When Emperor Gaozu slew the serpent, raised his righteous standard, and destroyed the tyrannical Qin, the realm passed from chaos into order. By the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, two hundred years had passed and peace had long endured; then Wang Mang usurped the throne and rebelled, and the realm passed once more from order into chaos. Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty and rebuilt its foundations, so that chaos gave way to order again. Another two hundred years have now passed, and the people have long known peace; therefore war has broken out on every side once more. This is precisely the time when order is turning into chaos; it cannot be settled all at once. If you would have Kongming mediate between Heaven and Earth and mend the fabric of the universe, I fear the task will not be easy and will merely consume your energies. Have you not heard, ‘He who follows Heaven finds ease; he who defies Heaven finds toil’? ‘Where destiny’s numbers are fixed, reason cannot wrest them away; where fate is ordained, man cannot bend it by force’?”

p.src: Xuande said, “Your words, sir, are indeed most discerning. Yet I, Bei, am a scion of the Han. It is my duty to uphold the imperial house; how could I dare abandon it all to destiny and fate?” Zhou Ping replied, “I am but a rustic of the hills, unworthy to discuss the affairs of the realm with you. I spoke rashly only because you honored me with your question.” Xuande said, “I am grateful for your instruction, sir, but do you know where Kongming has gone?” Zhou Ping replied, “I too wished to visit him, but I do not know where he has gone.” Xuande asked, “Would you come with me to my humble county?” Zhou Ping replied, “By nature I greatly delight in an idle, unfettered life, and I have long had no desire for rank or fame. Let us meet again another day.” With that, he gave a deep bow and departed. Xuande, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei mounted their horses and rode on. Zhang Fei said, “We failed to find Kongming again, and instead met this pedantic scholar and wasted so long in idle talk!” Xuande replied, “Those too were the words of a recluse.”

Why must you go yourself, brother? Just send someone to summon him here.” Xuande rebuked him. “Have you not heard Mencius say, ‘To wish to see a worthy man without observing the proper way is like wishing him to enter while shutting the door against him’? Kongming is one of the great worthies of our age. How could he be summoned?” He mounted his horse and set out once more to visit Kongming. Guan Yu and Zhang Fei also mounted and followed him.

p.src: When the two had finished singing, they clapped their hands and laughed heartily. Xuande said, “Could Sleeping Dragon be in there?” He dismounted and entered the tavern. He saw two men leaning against a table and drinking face-to-face. The man in the place of honor had a fair face and a long beard; the other had striking, venerable features. Xuande bowed and asked, “Which of you gentlemen is Master Sleeping Dragon?” The long-bearded man asked, “Who are you, sir? What business have you in seeking Sleeping Dragon?” Xuande replied, “I am Liu Bei. I wish to visit the master and seek from him the art of saving the age and bringing peace to the people.” The long-bearded man said, “We are not Sleeping Dragon; we are both his friends. I am Shi Guangyuan of Yingchuan, and this gentleman is Meng Gongwei of Runan.” Xuande said delightedly, “I have long heard of your great names, gentlemen, and count myself fortunate to meet you by chance. We have spare horses with us; may I invite you both to accompany us to Sleeping Dragon’s estate for a conversation?” Guangyuan replied, “We are all idle fellows of the wilds, ignorant of the business of governing the state and bringing peace to the people. You need not trouble to ask us. Please mount your horse, illustrious sir, and go seek Sleeping Dragon yourself.”

Guangyuan replied, “We are all idle fellows of the wilds, ignorant of the business of governing the state and bringing peace to the people. You need not trouble to ask us.
Please mount your horse, illustrious sir, and go seek Sleeping Dragon yourself.”

As the man rounded the little bridge, he chanted a poem.
The poem went:

p.src: When Xuande heard the song, he exclaimed, “This must truly be the Sleeping Dragon!” He swung down from the saddle, stepped forward, and bowed, saying, “It cannot have been easy for you, sir, to brave this cold! Liu Bei has been waiting for you a long while!” The man hurriedly dismounted from his donkey and returned the courtesy. Zhuge Jun, coming behind him, said, “This is not my elder brother, the Sleeping Dragon, but my brother’s father-in-law, Huang Chengyan.” Xuande said, “The verses you were reciting just now were exceedingly profound.” Chengyan replied, “At my son-in-law’s home I once read the ‘Liangfu Lament’ and happened to remember this piece; as I was crossing the little bridge just now, I chanced to see plum blossoms among the hedges and, moved by the sight, recited it. I did not expect my honored guests to overhear me.” Xuande asked, “Have you seen your worthy son-in-law?” Chengyan replied, “Why, I myself have come to see him.” Hearing this, Xuande took leave of Chengyan, mounted his horse, and set off homeward. Just then the wind and snow grew fiercer still; looking back toward Sleeping Dragon Ridge, he was overcome with dejection. p.src: After Xuande returned to Xinye, time slipped quietly by, and before long the new spring arrived. He ordered a diviner to cast yarrow stalks and choose an auspicious day; then, after fasting and purifying himself for three days, burning incense, bathing, and changing his garments, he prepared to go once more to Sleeping Dragon Ridge to pay his respects to Kongming. When Guan Yu and Zhang Fei heard of this, they were displeased and went together to remonstrate with Xuande. Indeed:
